big_picture: US stablecoin rules moved closer to taking effect this week: the OCC issued its final GENIUS Act rule (effective Jan 18, 2027), and comment periods on Treasury's GENIUS issuance rule and the SEC's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets both closed.

Banks and their partners kept putting regulated digital dollars onto public chains: JPMorgan's JPM Coin deposit token went live on Ethereum, and Cross River and DriveWealth both added Ripple's RLUSD on the XRP Ledger.
Global standard-setters (BIS, IMF) kept pushing the same message: tokenised deposits, regulated stablecoins and CBDCs should be interoperable and anchored to central bank money.

items.headline: OCC issues final GENIUS Act rule for payment stablecoin issuers; effective Jan 18, 2027. Treasury's GENIUS issuance NPRM closed for comment Oct 19
items.why_it_matters: Gives bank-chartered stablecoin issuers a clear compliance path covering reserves, redemption, custody and licensing. BSA/AML rules will follow separately, and the application start date has not been announced.
items.link_basis: Sector-wide US stablecoin rule; applies to regulated USD stablecoins such as RLUSD and USDC, names no token.

items.headline: Comment period on proposed Regulation Crypto Assets closes with 100+ submissions
items.why_it_matters: The final text will shape token classification and secondary trading. No timetable has been set and one letter asked for withdrawal. Separately, nine issuers used objection rights against tokenized trading of their shares on OKXICE.

items.headline: ANPRM on Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Crypto Asset Markets published in the Federal Register
items.why_it_matters: Starts a framework for retail leveraged and margined crypto trading, with comments due Dec 14. Agencies are writing their own rules while legislation stays stalled.

items.headline: JPM Coin (JPMD) USD deposit token goes live on Ethereum L1 for institutional clients
items.why_it_matters: A large bank is using public chains to settle deposit tokens. JPMorgan says Kinexys has processed over $4T cumulatively, averaging about $7B a day. JPMD also competes with public stablecoins.
items.link_basis: JPMorgan announced JPM Coin live on Ethereum.

items.headline: Cross River builds Ripple's RLUSD on the XRP Ledger into its core banking OS
items.why_it_matters: Fintechs get RLUSD alongside ACH, wires and real-time payments through one API. The release puts RLUSD above $2.5B market cap, with more than $1B on XRPL. Service is available only in limited states.
items.link_basis: Cross River announced RLUSD on the XRP Ledger in its core banking stack.

items.headline: DriveWealth partners with Ripple for RLUSD settlement, payments, custody and equity financing
items.why_it_matters: Brings stablecoin funding to brokerage infrastructure, starting in Europe with plans for the US. No launch date was given.
items.link_basis: Ripple and DriveWealth announced the partnership (RLUSD on XRPL settlement).

items.headline: SBI XDC Network APAC, SBI VC Trade and Shinhan Card sign MOU for a yen-stablecoin payment trial
items.why_it_matters: Proof of concept for cross-border yen-stablecoin card payments and trade settlement on XDC infrastructure. Any commercial launch depends on regulation in Japan and Korea.
items.link_basis: SBI XDC Network APAC is a named party to the MOU.

items.headline: XDC listed on Robinhood; Concordium selected as Know-Your-Agent layer
items.why_it_matters: Opens access to US retail investors and adds an identity layer for AI-agent payments.

items.headline: Bell (Protocol 30) upgrade announced: W-addresses, millisecond ledger timing, post-quantum signatures
items.why_it_matters: Lets institutions manage many customer balances through one smart contract. Testnet upgrades Nov 3; mainnet vote Nov 23.

items.headline: BIS publishes central-bank speeches on trusted digital money and interoperability (MAS keynote, Central Bank of Ireland)
items.why_it_matters: Treats deposit tokens, regulated stablecoins and CBDC as complementary, with a 'network of networks' linked by interoperability standards and agentic-finance safeguards.
items.link_basis: Lumi's analysis: the speeches describe a 'network of networks' of deposit tokens, stablecoins and CBDC linked by interoperability standards, which matches the stated missions of interoperable settlement networks (XRPL, Stellar, Hedera, XDC) and cross-chain messaging (Axelar). No token is named.

items.headline: G-24/AFI roundtable at the IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings focuses on proportionate crypto rules
items.why_it_matters: Emerging-market policymakers flagged stablecoin risks to monetary policy and financial integrity, a signal for future global rules.

items.headline: Governance proposal #499 passes; #500 (ITS batch migration) in voting through Oct 22
items.why_it_matters: Routine protocol maintenance; no major announcements.

connections.text: The OCC final rule and the closed Treasury comment period give bank-linked issuers a legal path. This week's Cross River and DriveWealth integrations show existing demand for regulated dollars on XRPL.
JPM Coin on Ethereum is the deposit-token model BIS/MAS describe for banking use cases. RLUSD and USDC fill the stablecoin role in fintech and on exchanges. Both settle on public chains.
BIS/MAS favour a multi-ledger world, which supports cross-chain messaging (AXL) and multi-rail issuers. No new ISO 20022-specific developments surfaced this week.
Issuer objections on OKXICE and the final Reg Crypto text will shape tokenized equity/treasury venues such as Securitize.
MAS SAFR, XDC's Know-Your-Agent layer and Hedera's x402-compatible Agent Accounts all point to AI-agent spending running on regulated stablecoins.
